messages:
julia_sales: SeaStar wants Private deployment into their transit VPC. Requirements: preserve client source IP for audit logs, allow TLS inspect in their DMZ, and they asked for a quick cost comparison: static EIP-per-AZ vs shared NAT. Need a short checklist they can hand to NetOps.

omar_se: Short summary: doable. If traffic is SNATed by a centralized TGW NAT you lose original IP. Options: PrivateLink ENIs that avoid SNAT, internal NLB with static EIP on our side, PROXY protocol/X-Forwarded-For from their DMZ proxy, or 1:1 SNAT (EIP per host). Each has tradeoffs on cost and HA.

avin_netops: Clarifying q: how will on-prem connect — Direct Connect -> TGW (hairpin likely) or VPN/SD-WAN into a spoke? That changes recommendations since TGW central NAT will SNAT by design.

julia_sales: They plan Direct Connect into a transit TGW for low latency. Ops still open to using PrivateLink for the service path. Security asks whether TLS inspect will break mTLS.

lina_sec: TLS-inspect note: allowed if customer retains keys and we terminate mTLS at the connector inside their VPC. We will not accept MITM of our control-plane certs. For Private deploy we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS. I'll draft SQ responses (min TLS1.2, preferred TLS1.3, ciphers list, mTLS flow, audit log retention options).

omar_se: Pasteable firewall snippet for their NetOps:

```
# Outbound rules (preferred: FQDN allowlist)
Allow TCP 443 -> *.redwood-private.<region>
Allow UDP 123 -> 0.0.0.0/0  # NTP
# Optional inbound if health probes used
Allow TCP 443 <- <redwood-health-ips>
```

Also: we publish IP ranges JSON in onboarding; prefer FQDN to avoid churn.

avin_netops: Practical src-IP preservation options:
- PrivateLink (interface ENIs) routed without SNAT -> preserves IP end-to-end.
- Internal NLB + static EIP -> upstream sees EIP but we can map flows to customer.
- DMZ proxy sending PROXY header or X-Forwarded-For -> app must consume header.
- 1:1 SNAT (per-host EIP) -> preserves mapping but higher cost and management.
Note: ALB typically requires proxy protocol to preserve source IP.

julia_sales: Pricing ask: ballpark monthly delta for per-AZ static EIP mapping vs shared NAT? Can we give a quick estimate to the buyer?

omar_se: Ballpark guidance: per-managed EIP add-on is a Private-deploy option, usually billed monthly per-EIP (order of magnitude: tens-to-low-hundreds USD per EIP/month depending on region and contract) plus egress. Shared NAT reduces infra cost but no sticky per-customer IP on failover. I'll confirm exact numbers with finance and add to the onboarding doc.

avin_netops: Ops callouts: watch MTU when IPsec/encapsulation exists (recommend PMTU ~1400), set TCP keepalive <60s for long streams, and document idle timeouts. Multi-region sticky egress failover is complex
—call it out as POC risk.

omar_se: Action items:
- Omar: one-pager decision matrix (PrivateLink vs TGW vs Peering) with src-IP tradeoffs + small diagram and PROXY header example (eg: "PROXY TCP4 198.51.100.23 10.0.0.5 443 51324\n").
- Navin: DMZ proxy config snippet + MTU/keepalive ops note.
- Lina: security questionnaire answers (mTLS/KMS/audit logging).
- Julia: confirm buyer preference and whether they can accept PROXY headers or require per-EIP.

julia_sales: I'll run this with SeaStar tomorrow and share the one-pager. Please drop artifacts in the onboarding link. Thanks all :thumbsup:
